<p id="A3.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where the final step follows from the identity</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\mathbf{x}}\log p({\mathbf{x}};\sigma)=({\mathbf{D}}({\mathbf{x}};\sigma)-{\mathbf{x}})/\sigma^{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐃</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\mathbf{x}}\log p({\mathbf{x}};\sigma)=({\mathbf{D}}({\mathbf{x}};\sigma)-{\mathbf{x}})/\sigma^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite>. Using this, the optimal velocity from flow matching, <math id="A3.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{v}}^{*}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{v}}^{*}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)</annotation></semantics></math>, can be computed as</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{v}}^{*}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)=\mathbb{E}[{\mathbf{x}}_{1}-{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\mid{\mathbf{x}}_{t}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{{\mathbf{x}}_{t}-{\mathbf{x}}_{0}}{t}\mid{\mathbf{x}}_{t}\right]=\frac{{\mathbf{x}}_{t}}{t}-\frac{1}{t}\mathbb{E}[{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\mid{\mathbf{x}}_{t}]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐯</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{v}}^{*}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)=\mathbb{E}[{\mathbf{x}}_{1}-{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\mid{\mathbf{x}}_{t}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\frac{{\mathbf{x}}_{t}-{\mathbf{x}}_{0}}{t}\mid{\mathbf{x}}_{t}\right]=\frac{{\mathbf{x}}_{t}}{t}-\frac{1}{t}\mathbb{E}[{\mathbf{x}}_{0}\mid{\mathbf{x}}_{t}].</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">

<p id="A3.SS1.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">Consider the non-optimal consistency model</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text">Note that <math id="A3.SS1.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{f}}_{\epsilon}({\mathbf{x}},0)={\mathbf{x}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐟</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>𝐱</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{f}}_{\epsilon}({\mathbf{x}},0)={\mathbf{x}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies the boundary condition and is a valid consistency model.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let us analyze a single multistep transition from timestep <math id="A3.SS1.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> to timestep <math id="A3.SS1.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>. This process consists of two steps:
1. The noise is removed by predicting the clean data using the consistency model, yielding <math id="A3.SS1.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{\prime}_{0}={\mathbf{f}}_{\epsilon}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐟</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}^{\prime}_{0}={\mathbf{f}}_{\epsilon}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
2. The estimated clean data <math id="A3.SS1.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}^{\prime}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}^{\prime}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is then noised back to timestep <math id="A3.SS1.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> using</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{s}=s\times{\mathbf{z}}+(1-s)\times{\mathbf{x}}^{\prime}_{0},\quad{\mathbf{z}}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},{\mathbf{I}})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>𝐳</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>𝐳</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>𝐈</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{s}=s\times{\mathbf{z}}+(1-s)\times{\mathbf{x}}^{\prime}_{0},\quad{\mathbf{z}}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},{\mathbf{I}}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">Assuming that <math id="A3.SS1.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{t}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\sigma_{t}^{2}{\mathbf{I}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>𝟎</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝐈</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{t}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\sigma_{t}^{2}{\mathbf{I}})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{x}}_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{x}}_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> will also follow an isotropic zero-mean Gaussian distribution and is obtained as follows:</span></p>

<p id="A3.SS1.p10.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p10.2.1" class="ltx_text">Therefore, the variance of <math id="A3.SS1.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{s}</annotation></semantics></math> is given by</span></p>

</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">Using this recurrence relation, we can compute the variance of the distribution obtained by running multistep CM sampling on a uniform <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-step schedule:</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,\frac{1}{n},\dots,\frac{n-1}{n},1]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,\frac{1}{n},\dots,\frac{n-1}{n},1].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p11.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p11.2.1" class="ltx_text">Since both the ground truth distribution and the distribution of <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>x</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> derived by <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-step sampling are isotropic zero-mean Gaussians, the Wasserstein-2 distance between them has the following closed form solution:</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex24" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{2}(p({\mathbf{x}}_{0});p_{data}({\mathbf{x}}))=(\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}({\mathbf{x}}_{0})}-c)^{2}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>𝐱</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msqrt><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{2}(p({\mathbf{x}}_{0});p_{data}({\mathbf{x}}))=(\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}({\mathbf{x}}_{0})}-c)^{2}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p11.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p11.3.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(s):=\operatorname{Var}({\mathbf{x}}_{s})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>s</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(s):=\operatorname{Var}({\mathbf{x}}_{s})</annotation></semantics></math> for convenience. We will show that as <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, the variance <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(0)</annotation></semantics></math> when computed via the recurrence defined in <a href="#A3.E8" title="In Proof. ‣ C.1 Theorem: Consistency Models are Flawed Multi-step Generators ‣ Appendix C Proofs, Derivations and Theoretical Details ‣ Appendix ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> on the uniform <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> step schedule diverges, i.e. <math id="A3.SS1.p11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}(0)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}(0)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>. This means performing multi-step sampling with the consistency model will result in accumulated errors beyond a certain point.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p12.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p12.1.1" class="ltx_text">Define</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(s):=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(s)}{s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}c^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(s):=\frac{\operatorname{Var}(s)}{s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}c^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p12.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p12.2.1" class="ltx_text">Plugging this into <a href="#A3.E8" title="In Proof. ‣ C.1 Theorem: Consistency Models are Flawed Multi-step Generators ‣ Appendix C Proofs, Derivations and Theoretical Details ‣ Appendix ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> gives:</span></p>
<table id="A3.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(s)=\frac{s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}(c+t\epsilon)^{2}h(t)}{s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}c^{2}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(s)=\frac{s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}(c+t\epsilon)^{2}h(t)}{s^{2}+(1-s)^{2}c^{2}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p12.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p12.3.1" class="ltx_text">We know <math id="A3.SS1.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(1)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(1)=1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(0)=\operatorname{Var}(0)/c^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Var</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>c</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(0)=\operatorname{Var}(0)/c^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. So, it’s enough to show that <math id="A3.SS1.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(0)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(0)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS1.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p13.1.1" class="ltx_text">It’s easy to see by induction that <math id="A3.SS1.p13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h(t)\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(t)\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Define <math id="A3.SS1.p13.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(t):=h(t)-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(t):=h(t)-1</annotation></semantics></math> to measure how much it grows. Then:</span></p>
<table id="A3.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<div id="A3.SS1.p14" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p14.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p14.1.1" class="ltx_text">All terms are positive, so let’s lower bound <math id="A3.SS1.p14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(t)</annotation></semantics></math> by defining a simpler sequence:</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="A3.SS1.p14.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p14.2.1" class="ltx_text">Clearly <math id="A3.SS1.p14.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(s)\geq g^{\prime}(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(s)\geq g^{\prime}(s)</annotation></semantics></math>, so it’s enough to show <math id="A3.SS1.p14.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{\prime}(0)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{\prime}(0)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS1.p14.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p15" class="ltx_para">

<p id="A3.SS1.p15.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p15.3.1" class="ltx_text">with <math id="A3.SS1.p15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(1)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(1)=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(0)=g^{\prime}(0)/(2c\epsilon)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(0)=g^{\prime}(0)/(2c\epsilon)</annotation></semantics></math>. So we just need to show <math id="A3.SS1.p15.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(0)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(0)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS1.p15.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>

</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p16.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p16.3.1" class="ltx_text">Subtracting <math id="A3.SS1.p16.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(s,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(s,t)</annotation></semantics></math> from both sides, we get:</span></p>
<table id="A3.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p16.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p16.4.1" class="ltx_text">where:</span></p>
<table id="A3.Ex27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.Ex27.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(s):=\frac{1}{(\frac{s}{(1-s)c})^{2}+1}&lt;1." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(s):=\frac{1}{(\frac{s}{(1-s)c})^{2}+1}&lt;1.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p17" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p17.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p17.1.1" class="ltx_text">So <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{s,t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{s,t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> pulls every point toward its fixed point <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(s,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(s,t)</annotation></semantics></math>, with a pull factor of <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(s)</annotation></semantics></math>. As <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, since <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(s,t)\geq\frac{(1-s)^{2}}{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>s</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(s,t)\geq\frac{(1-s)^{2}}{s}</annotation></semantics></math>, the fixed point <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(s,t)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(s,t)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, and the pull factor <math id="A3.SS1.p17.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda(s)</annotation></semantics></math> approaches 1, meaning the pull gets weaker.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p18" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p18.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p18.1.1" class="ltx_text">This means the recurrence in <a href="#A3.E12" title="In Proof. ‣ C.1 Theorem: Consistency Models are Flawed Multi-step Generators ‣ Appendix C Proofs, Derivations and Theoretical Details ‣ Appendix ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> is applying a sequence of weaker and weaker pulls toward bigger and bigger targets. To prove <math id="A3.SS1.p18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(0)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(0)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, we now proceed by contradiction. Assume there exists some <math id="A3.SS1.p18.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and an infinite sequence <math id="A3.SS1.p18.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n_{1}&lt;n_{2}&lt;\dots" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n_{1}&lt;n_{2}&lt;\dots</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="A3.SS1.p18.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(0)&lt;\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(0)&lt;\delta</annotation></semantics></math> when using the schedule <math id="A3.SS1.p18.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,\tfrac{1}{n_{i}},\dots,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>n</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,\tfrac{1}{n_{i}},\dots,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p19" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p19.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p19.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(s,t)\geq\frac{(1-s)^{2}}{s}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>s</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(s,t)\geq\frac{(1-s)^{2}}{s}</annotation></semantics></math> and the function <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{(1-x)^{2}}{x}\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(1-x)^{2}}{x}\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, we can pick <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{*}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{*}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> such that for all <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in[0,t^{*}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in[0,t^{*}]</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></p>
<table id="A3.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{(1-t^{*})^{2}}{t^{*}}=2\delta\Rightarrow o(s,t)\geq\frac{(1-s)^{2}}{s}\geq 2\delta." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⇒</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>s</mi></mfrac><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{(1-t^{*})^{2}}{t^{*}}=2\delta\Rightarrow o(s,t)\geq\frac{(1-s)^{2}}{s}\geq 2\delta.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p19.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p19.2.1" class="ltx_text">So every fixed point in <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,t^{*}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,t^{*}]</annotation></semantics></math> is at least <math id="A3.SS1.p19.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p20" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p20.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p20.1.1" class="ltx_text">Now we split the problem into two cases:</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p21" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p21.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p21.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case 1<span id="A3.SS1.p21.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">: There exists some <math id="A3.SS1.p21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in[0,t^{*}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in[0,t^{*}]</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A3.SS1.p21.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(s)\geq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(s)\geq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>. Since all future pulls are toward values <math id="A3.SS1.p21.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="&gt;2\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">&gt;2\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.SS1.p21.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> will stay above <math id="A3.SS1.p21.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math id="A3.SS1.p21.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(0)\geq\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(0)\geq\delta</annotation></semantics></math>—a contradiction.</span></span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p22" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p22.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p22.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Case 2<span id="A3.SS1.p22.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium">: For all <math id="A3.SS1.p22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\in[0,t^{*}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\in[0,t^{*}]</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="A3.SS1.p22.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(s)&lt;\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(s)&lt;\delta</annotation></semantics></math>.
Pick any <math id="A3.SS1.p22.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{*}\in(0,t^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{*}\in(0,t^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>. Let <math id="A3.SS1.p22.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell:=\lambda(s^{*})&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell:=\lambda(s^{*})&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, which is the maximum pull factor (corresponding to the weakest pull) on <math id="A3.SS1.p22.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[s^{*},t^{*}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[s^{*},t^{*}]</annotation></semantics></math>. Then for <math id="A3.SS1.p22.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{*}\leq s&lt;t\leq t^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>≤</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{*}\leq s&lt;t\leq t^{*}</annotation></semantics></math>:</span></span></p>
<table id="A3.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A3.Ex28"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex28.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle 2\delta-r(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle 2\delta-r(s)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.Ex28.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=(o(s,t)-r(s))" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=(o(s,t)-r(s))</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="A3.SS1.p23" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p23.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p23.1.1" class="ltx_text">Applying this inequality <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> times (where <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of steps between <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> on the schedule), we get:</span></p>
<table id="A3.E17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A3.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\leq 2\delta-r(s^{*})\leq 2\delta\ell^{M}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>M</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\leq 2\delta-r(s^{*})\leq 2\delta\ell^{M}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS1.p23.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p23.2.1" class="ltx_text">If <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is large enough so that <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\delta\ell^{M}&lt;\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>M</mi></msup></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\delta\ell^{M}&lt;\delta</annotation></semantics></math>, we get a contradiction. This happens when <math id="A3.SS1.p23.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n&gt;M/(t^{*}-s^{*})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>/</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n&gt;M/(t^{*}-s^{*})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p24" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p24.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p24.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since both cases lead to a contradiction, we conclude that <math id="A3.SS1.p24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(0)\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(0)\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="A3.SS1.p24.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, completing the proof.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p25" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p25.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p25.1.1" class="ltx_text">∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A3.SS1.p26" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS1.p26.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS1.p26.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Intuition:</span> When doing multi-step sampling with consistency models we first perform denoising by removing all noise from a noisy image to obtain a clean one, and then re-add a smaller amount of noise. But because the model is not perfect, the denoised image drifts slightly off the true data manifold. When noise is added back in, the resulting image is now slightly off the noisy manifold the model was trained on. This mismatch compounds: each denoising step starts from a slightly worse input, pushing the sample further off-manifold over time. As a result, errors accumulate with more sampling steps, leading to degrading image quality beyond a certain point.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.2 </span>Theorems: Flow Map Objectives</h4>

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.1 </span>AYF-EMD
</h5>

<div id="A3.Thmtheorem2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem C.2</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Restated from <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Proof in Appendix). ‣ 3.2 Learning Flow Maps ‣ 3 Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a>)<span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{f}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐟</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{f}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)</annotation></semantics></math> be the flow map and <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)</annotation></semantics></math> denote the pretrained flow matching model. Define <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{-}=\text{stopgrad}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">stopgrad</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{-}=\text{stopgrad}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\prime}=t+\epsilon(s-t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\prime}=t+\epsilon(s-t)</annotation></semantics></math> denote two adjacent starting timesteps for a small <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\prime}\in[t,s]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\prime}\in[t,s]</annotation></semantics></math> is derived by taking a small step from <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> towards <math id="A3.Thmtheorem2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>.
Consider the following consistency loss function defined</span></p>

<div id="A3.Thmtheorem3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary C.3</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Proof in Appendix). ‣ 3.2 Learning Flow Maps ‣ 3 Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a><span id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> assumes that the step size is proportional to the interval length, i.e. <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|t-t^{\prime}|\propto|t-s|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|t-t^{\prime}|\propto|t-s|</annotation></semantics></math>, leading to the introduction of a <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t-s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t-s)</annotation></semantics></math> term in the weighting function. This can be eliminated by using <math id="A3.Thmtheorem3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\prime}=t+sign(s-t)\times\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\prime}=t+sign(s-t)\times\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> and leads to the following objective:</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<section id="A3.SS2.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">C.2.2 </span>AYF-LMD
</h5>

<div id="A3.Thmtheorem4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_theorem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem C.4</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Restated from <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3.3 (Proof in Appendix). ‣ 3.2 Learning Flow Maps ‣ 3 Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a>)<span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{f}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐟</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{f}}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)</annotation></semantics></math> be the flow map, <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)</annotation></semantics></math> be the pretrained flow matching model, and define <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta^{-}=\text{stopgrad}(\theta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic">stopgrad</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta^{-}=\text{stopgrad}(\theta)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Let <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}=s+\epsilon(t-s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}=s+\epsilon(t-s)</annotation></semantics></math> denote two adjacent ending timesteps for a small <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Note that <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}\in[t,s]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}\in[t,s]</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained by taking a small step from <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> towards <math id="A3.Thmtheorem4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.

<div id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Taking the limit of both sides as <math id="A3.SS2.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> completes the proof.
∎</span></p>

<div id="A3.Thmtheorem5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_corollary">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="A3.Thmtheorem5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary C.5</span></span><span id="A3.Thmtheorem5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="A3.Thmtheorem5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><a href="#S3.Thmtheorem3" title="Theorem 3.3 (Proof in Appendix). ‣ 3.2 Learning Flow Maps ‣ 3 Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref ltx_font_italic"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.3</span></a><span id="A3.Thmtheorem5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> assumes that the step size is proportional to the interval length, i.e. <math id="A3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|s-s^{\prime}|\propto|t-s|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>∝</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|s-s^{\prime}|\propto|t-s|</annotation></semantics></math>, leading to the introduction of a <math id="A3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t-s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t-s)</annotation></semantics></math> term in the weighting function. This can be eliminated by using <math id="A3.Thmtheorem5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s^{\prime}=s+sign(t-s)\times\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>s</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s^{\prime}=s+sign(t-s)\times\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> which leads to the following objective:</span></p>
<table id="A3.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<section id="A3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">C.3 </span>Derivation: Tangent Warmup as Linearity Regularization
</h4>

<div id="A3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Here, we derive <a href="#S3.E5" title="In Regularized Tangent Warmup ‣ 3.4 Training Tricks ‣ 3 Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Eq.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>. stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\stackrel{{\scriptstyle(iii)}}{{=}}\left(\nabla_{\theta}[\mathbf{F}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)-{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)]\right)\times\left(\mathbf{F}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)-{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)\right)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr>
<tr id="A3.E24Xg" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A3.E24Xg.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=0.5\times\nabla_{\theta}\|\mathbf{F}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)-{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)\|_{2}^{2}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐅</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=0.5\times\nabla_{\theta}\|\mathbf{F}_{\theta}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)-{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t,s)\|_{2}^{2},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where (i) is because we discard <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|t-s|\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|t-s|\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, which doesn’t change the gradient direction, (ii) is because <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{F}_{\theta}=\mathbf{F}_{\theta^{-}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐅</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐅</mi><msup><mi>θ</mi><mo>−</mo></msup></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{F}_{\theta}=\mathbf{F}_{\theta^{-}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and (iii) is because <math id="A3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla_{\theta}{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∇</mo><mi>θ</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝐯</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐱</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla_{\theta}{\mathbf{v}}_{\phi}({\mathbf{x}}_{t},t)=0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Connections to Existing Methods</h3>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we highlight the connections between AYF and existing methods. We show how AYF generalizes several prior approaches and discuss its relationship to recent concurrent works. See <a href="#A4.F9" title="In Appendix D Connections to Existing Methods ‣ Appendix ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Fig.</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> for a schematic overview of these connections. In the following subsections, we will derive these relationships in detail.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A4.F9" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2506.14603v1/figures/ayf_generalizes_all_v2.jpg" id="A4.F9.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:357/202;" width="357" height="202" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="A4.F9.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 9</span>: </span><span id="A4.F9.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">AYF can be seen a a generalization of many prior works such as Flow Matching <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, Continuous-time Consistency Models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, Flow Map Matching <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, Consistency Trajectory Distillation <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib93" title="" class="ltx_ref">93</a>]</cite>, and the concurrent MeanFlow Models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Flow Matching</h4>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We show that the AYF-EMD objective introduced in <a href="#S3.Thmtheorem2" title="Theorem 3.2 (Proof in Appendix). ‣ 3.2 Learning Flow Maps ‣ 3 Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation ‣ Align Your Flow:Scaling Continuous-Time Flow Map Distillation" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">Theorem</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.2</span></a> generalizes the standard flow matching objective. In particular, we prove that the gradient of the AYF-EMD objective reduces to the flow matching gradient in the limit as <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s\to t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s\to t</annotation></semantics></math>, up to a constant factor.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Recall the flow map parameterization:</p>
<table id="A4.E25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">
